To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a novel risk factor-based HF subphenotyping schema, and that subphenotyping by CHD or metabolic syndromes is associated with greater mortality risk.

(1) HF subphenotypes are characterized by the presence or absence of CHD and metabolic syndrome, (2) the presence of these risk factors at the time of HF onset is associated with a younger age at onset and worse prognosis, and (3) several echocardiography and vascular indices worsen in the presence of these cardiovascular risk factors, even in a sample without overt HF
we have proposed a subphenotyping system for HF based on risk factors and that the subphenotypes are marked by varying mortality and distinct clinical features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of subgroups of HF, and their relationship to risk factors.
the identification of risk factors for cardiovascular disease in a community based sample.
the development of subphenotypes of heart failure (HF) and the assessment of their prognostic significance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subphenotyping of HF based on the presence of CHF risk factors is a promising approach, but that more research is needed.
the subphenotyping of HF based on the presence of CHF, CHD or metabolic risk factors, and hypertension, is associated with different mortality rates.
the presence of coronary heart disease or metabolic syndrome in patients with heart failure, with or without preserved ejection fraction, portends a worse prognosis than the other two subgroups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HF subtypes characterized by coronary artery disease or metabolic syndrome present earlier in life and are marked by a worse prognosis.
HF is a heterogeneous syndrome with varying risk factors and prognosis.
the presence of CHF in the context of coronary heart disease or the metabolic syndrome is associated with greater risk of mortality than CHF in the setting of hypertension or obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HF is a heterogeneous clinical entity, with different risk factors contributing to its development.
the subphenotypes of HF are associated with different risk factors and mortality.
HF subphenotyping is feasible and can be used to study the natural history and outcomes of the HF syndrome.
